pending.title: Claim: The 50% CGT discount is being replaced by cost base indexation
pending.description: [SOURCE URL MAY NOT CONTAIN CLAIM — verify before publishing] Multiple commercial sources (NAB, etc.) describe the CGT reform as replacing the 50% discount with 'cost base indexation.' However, the official budget.gov.au states the reform will introduce 'a discount based on inflation.' These are technically different mechanisms: indexation adjusts the purchase price for inflation (applied at time of sale), while an inflation-based discount applies a discount to gains attributable to inflation. This distinction could result in different tax outcomes for investors, and media may be oversimplifying the actual reform mechanism.
pending.suggestion: Add to fact-checks.json: claim is 'replaced by cost base indexation', verdict is partially_true/disputed because the official budget describes an 'inflation-based discount' which may work differently from traditional cost base indexation. The exact calculation method is subject to legislation.
